text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The army's number two says the military has no interest in governing the country but calls on the government to implement series of anti-Islamist measures.
- The World Bank places Turkey among the top ten developing countries.
- Rival far-right militants mourning death of nationalist leader Alpaslan Turkes fight amongst themselves.
- British paper Daily Telegraph says Turkey has the second-highest number of homosexuals in the world.
- Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller protects two of her MPs who have been accused of deep involvement in a security scandal.
- The crisis over the appointment of a new police chief mounts as President Suleyman Demirel rejects signing the decree for it.
- The trade deficit increased by 57.4 percent in the first half of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995.
- Member of a parliamanetary inquiry into a security scandal says the intelligence service should be monitored by parliament.
